claims: The Orion capsule is NASA’s crewed spacecraft.
The Orion capsule is designed for deep space exploration including the Artemis lunar missions and future missions to Mars.
The Orion capsule was developed with Lockheed Martin.
The Orion capsule carries four astronauts.
The Orion capsule provides advanced radiation protection.
The Orion capsule is part of a larger system including ESA's Service Module.
The Orion capsule successfully returned from the Moon in April 2026.
The Orion capsule is designed for long-duration deep space missions up to 21 days or longer with habitat modules.
The Orion capsule is designed for safe return from the Moon.
The Orion capsule contains 330 cubic feet of space.
The Orion capsule has 57% more space than the Apollo capsule.
The Orion capsule accommodates four crew members with a private hygiene bay.
The Orion capsule is equipped with advanced heat shielding.
The Orion capsule is designed to withstand re-entry speeds of roughly 32,000 km/h.
The Orion capsule is designed to withstand temperatures near 2700 ∘C.
The Orion capsule features advanced life support systems.
The Orion capsule consists of the Crew Module built by Lockheed Martin, the Crew Module Adapter, and the European Service Module (ESM).
The European Service Module (ESM) provides power and propulsion.
The Orion capsule uses a parachute system for water-based Pacific Ocean splashdown recovery.
The Orion capsule's recovery was seen in the Artemis II mission.
The Orion spacecraft functions autonomously during transit.
The Orion spacecraft includes full manual controls for crew intervention.
